a string element's enum members are strings
an integer element's enum members, minimum and maximum are integers
a number element's enum members are numbers
a boolean element's enum members are booleans

gasFeesPaidBy.description: Who the contract owner offers to have pay the gas (storage and processing fee) of this token-paid action: 0 - DocumentOwner (default, the contract owner never pays), 1 - ContractOwner (pays, and accepts every request), 2 - PreferContractOwner (pays when their balance covers the fee, but refuses a transition that insists on them). The transition asks with the same values in $tokenPaymentInfo.gasFeesPaidBy: DocumentOwner always pays itself, PreferContractOwner is accepted by every offer, and ContractOwner is accepted only by offer 1, else the transition is rejected (GasFeesPaidByNotAllowedError, code 40129). Acted on from protocol version 14; a failed transition is always paid for by its signer.

optional.description: True if a transition may leave $tokenPaymentInfo out for this action and pay no token, in which case its signer pays the gas in credits as for an action without a token cost and no gas sponsorship applies; with $tokenPaymentInfo present the token is charged exactly as for a required cost, and an insufficient token balance is a rejection, never a fallback to credits. Default false: the token payment is required (RequiredTokenPaymentInfoNotSetError, code 40115). Available from protocol version 14.

owner.description: Credits added to the contract's owner pot, which the contract owner claims.

moderators.description: Credits added to the contract's moderators pot, which the contract's moderation team shares equally. Requires the contract config to declare moderation.

resolution.description: Resolution. 0 - Masternode Vote. 1 - Masternode Vote without a Lock choice: the contest always ends with a winner, a tie goes to the earliest contender, and a contest with a single contender at the end of the join window is awarded at once

oneOf.description: Legacy form. true == "countable", false == "notCountable". Kept for back-compat with contracts written before the enum form was introduced.

"countable" — index uses a CountTree (O(1) totals). "countableAllowingOffset" — index uses a ProvableCountTree (totals + future O(log n) range / offset queries). "notCountable" — plain NormalTree (no count fast path).

countable.description: Whether and how the index supports count fast paths. Adds extra storage cost for non-default values.

rangeCountable.description: When true, the property-name level becomes a ProvableCountTree and value trees become CountTrees so range-count queries on the indexed property are O(log n). Implies `countable: "countable"` when `countable` is omitted, as the doctype-level `rangeCountable` implies `documentsCountable`; an explicit `"countableAllowingOffset"` is kept, and an explicit `"notCountable"` is rejected as a contradiction.

summable.description: Name of an integer document property whose values are aggregated into a sum at the index. When set, the index's value trees become SumTrees and each per-document index reference is a ReferenceWithSumItem contributing the named property's value to ancestor sum-bearing trees. The property must exist on the document type, be in `required`, and have an integer type. It must be a top-level property: the value is read from the top level of the document, so a dotted path to a property nested in an object is refused (from protocol version 14).

rangeSummable.description: When true, the property-name level becomes a ProvableSumTree (or ProvableCountProvableSumTree when paired with `rangeCountable: true`) so range-sum queries on the indexed property are O(log n) via the `AggregateSumOnRange` proof primitive. Requires `summable` to be set; `averageable` satisfies this, since it implies `summable`.

averageable.description: Syntactic sugar: `averageable: "<prop>"` is shorthand for `countable: "countable"` + `summable: "<prop>"`. Enables average queries (which return `(count, sum)` pairs the client divides) without forcing authors to think in terms of count + sum. Same on-disk layout as setting both underlying flags. If you set both `averageable` and `summable`, they must name the same property. Like `summable`, it names a top-level property, never a dotted path (from protocol version 14).

rangeAverageable.description: Syntactic sugar: `rangeAverageable: true` is shorthand for `rangeCountable: true` + `rangeSummable: true`. Requires `averageable` to be set.

oneOf.description: When true, the index's terminal property-name tree also carries an ordered secondary tree keyed by each group's document count, so "top / bottom K groups by count" queries are O(log n + k) with proofs. On a summableOffCountIndex index the document count is its sums, so this declares the Sum ranking (as rankedSummable does).

at.description: Name of the index property (or array of properties) whose levels carry Count rankings. Each must be one of the index's properties (an index has at most 10, hence maxItems); naming the last property is equivalent to the boolean form. A non-terminal property places a ranking at that prefix level: its values are ranked by whole-subtree document count (e.g. on [hashtag, postId], at: "hashtag" ranks hashtags by total count across all their posts), and every level from the shallowest ranked one down to the terminal is laid out count-bearing so each write's delta propagates up through the chain. ANY subset of levels may be named — e.g. ["hashtag", "postId"] declares both rankings on one index, and a fully ranked index ranks every level.

oneOf.description: Level-addressed form: places Count rankings at the named properties' levels. Cannot be combined with rankedSummable or rankedAverageable when a non-terminal level is named, except on a summableOffCountIndex index, and no other index of the document type may share a non-terminal ranked level or any level below it. On a summableOffCountIndex index a document count is its sums, so rankedCountable (either form) declares the same ranking as rankedSummable and needs no rangeCountable.

rankedCountable.description: Count ranking axis. Requires `rangeCountable: true`, except on a summableOffCountIndex index, where it is the Sum ranking. Independent of the Sum and Avg axes (`rankedSummable` / `rankedAverageable`), which take the level-addressed form only on a summableOffCountIndex index.

oneOf.description: When true, the index's terminal property-name tree also carries an ordered secondary tree keyed by each group's sum of the `summable` property (on a summableOffCountIndex index, of the source index's entries), so "top / bottom K groups by sum" queries are O(log n + k) with proofs. Requires `rangeSummable: true` (or `rangeAverageable: true`, which implies it). Adds the Sum ranking axis only.

at.description: Name of the index property (or array of properties) whose levels carry Sum rankings. Each must be one of the index's properties; naming the last property is equivalent to the boolean form. A non-terminal property ranks that property's values by the total of the counters beneath them.

oneOf.description: Level-addressed form, only on a summableOffCountIndex index: places Sum rankings at the named properties' levels.

rankedSummable.description: Sum ranking axis. Requires `rangeSummable: true`. The level-addressed form is only allowed on a summableOffCountIndex index.

oneOf.description: When true, the index's terminal property-name tree also carries an ordered secondary tree keyed by each group's average (count + sum pair) of the `averageable` property, so "top / bottom K groups by average" queries are O(log n + k) with proofs. Requires `rangeAverageable: true` (which itself implies `rangeCountable` + `rangeSummable`), or the explicit `rangeCountable: true` + `rangeSummable: true` pair. Adds the Avg ranking axis only — it does NOT imply `rankedCountable` or `rankedSummable`; each ranking axis costs its own secondary tree and is opted into separately.

at.description: Name of the index property (or array of properties) whose levels carry Avg rankings. Each must be one of the index's properties; naming the last property is equivalent to the boolean form. A non-terminal property ranks that property's values by the average per group of the counters beneath them.

oneOf.description: Level-addressed form, only on a summableOffCountIndex index: places Avg rankings at the named properties' levels.

rankedAverageable.description: Avg ranking axis. Requires `rangeCountable: true` and `rangeSummable: true`. The level-addressed form is only allowed on a summableOffCountIndex index.

on.description: Name of the timestamp index property to bucket. Must be this index's first property and name one of the system timestamps ($createdAt, $updatedAt or $transferredAt). A timeRange index may be unique only when range equals step (non-overlapping windows) and `on` is $createdAt.

range.description: Length of each time range window, in seconds. Must be an exact multiple of `step`.

step.description: Interval between successive range starts, in seconds. When `range` > `step` the ranges overlap and a document is indexed under `range / step` bucket-start values, bounded by a protocol-versioned cap (24 at protocol version 14).

phase.description: Grid alignment phase, in seconds. Range starts are `phase + k * step`; must be strictly less than `step` (a larger value would be a redundant spelling of `phase % step`) and strictly less than one year (31536000 — a phase further out could sit past current block time on a huge step, leaving valid timestamps before the grid's first bucket). A pure alignment offset — it moves where window boundaries fall (e.g. daily windows cut at 06:00 UTC instead of midnight) and never excludes any real timestamp. Defaults to 0.

ttl.description: Time to live, in seconds: entries under this index exist for at most this long past their bucket's start, plus a bounded drainage lag — every write into the index continues draining the oldest expired bucket under a per-write operation budget, and expired windows are not queryable (a byStart selection past the horizon is rejected), so every queryable window is complete. Must be at least `range` (a window still able to receive consensus-timestamped writes can never expire) and at most a protocol-versioned cap (604800 — one week — at protocol version 14). Indexes bucketing one field with the same grid share its storage level and must declare the same ttl. Bytes written under a TTL'd index bill to processing at an ephemeral-bytes rate instead of to storage, carry no storage flags, and refund nothing on removal. Omitted means entries live forever. Available from protocol version 14.

timeRange.description: Buckets the first index property's timestamp into fixed-length, regularly-spaced (possibly overlapping) time ranges. The window parameters (`range`, `step`, `phase`) are declared in seconds, since a bucket is selected from block time and the target block interval is five seconds; the stored key is the range start as a u64 millisecond timestamp, so it stays directly comparable to the source timestamp it buckets. Enables trending/leaderboard queries within the newest/oldest active range. A system-timestamp source must be listed in the document type's required fields. Several indexes may bucket the same timestamp with different grids — each grid gets its own index subtree, keyed by the property name qualified with the grid parameters. Available from protocol version 14.

on.description: Name of the integer property to bucket. Must be this index's first property, an integer property of the document type of at most 64 bits, and listed in the document type's required fields. An integerRange index may be unique only when range equals step (non-overlapping windows).

range.description: Length of each window, in the property's own units. Must be an exact multiple of `step`.

step.description: Interval between successive window starts. When `range` > `step` the windows overlap and a document is indexed under `range / step` window starts, bounded by a protocol-versioned cap (24 at protocol version 14).

phase.description: Grid alignment: window starts are `phase + k * step` for every integer k. Must be strictly less than `step`. Defaults to 0.

integerRange.description: Buckets the first index property's integer value into fixed-length, regularly-spaced (possibly overlapping) windows; a document is indexed under the start of every window containing its value, stored like a value of the property. A window that would start below the lowest value the property's integer type holds (0 for a property with a non-negative minimum) starts at that value instead, so every value is in at least one window. Queries select one window by its start with an IN_INTEGER_RANGE clause, and the index's counts, sums and rankings are then per window. Several indexes may bucket the same property with different grids; each grid gets its own index subtree. Cannot be combined with timeRange, and not allowed on indexOnly document types. Available from protocol version 14.

terminal.description: Only on indexOnly document types: the property, or the ordered list of properties (a composite terminal), whose encoded values, concatenated, are this index entry's member key — the docId-analog terminal key under the index's storage marker, stored as an Item instead of a Reference because there is no primary-storage row. Each component is "$ownerId" (the default when the keyword is omitted) or any schema property a prefix position could carry (no arrays or objects; byte arrays of at most 255 bytes, strings of at most 63 characters); every component but the last must be fixed width (a byte array with minItems equal to maxItems, an identifier, an integer, a boolean or a date), and the whole key at most 255 bytes. One entry exists per (prefix values, terminal values). No other system property may be a component, and none may repeat one of the index's listed properties. An index with no properties is a flat index keyed by its terminal alone, admitting no aggregate, ranking, timeRange, integerRange, skipIfAbsent or preallocated keyword. Available from protocol version 14.

preallocated.description: Only on indexOnly document types whose index path is fully determined by a same-contract permanentDocument or moderatedDocument refersTo declaration: every index property must be either the referring property itself (its value is the referenced document's $id) or a referring value of that declaration's where (consensus-equal to a referenced-document property; through moderatedDocument, the referenced $ownerId or a property the referenced type keeps under moderatorAbilities.deleteKeepsFields). When true, creating a referenced document also creates this index's dynamic trees for entries referencing it — paid by the referenced document's creator — and deleting the last entry keeps them, so every entry insert costs the same as the first. Available from protocol version 14.

outlivesDelete.description: Only on a timeRange index with a ttl of an indexOnly document type, without a sum and on a type without entryPayload: a delete of a document leaves its entries in this index to expire with their window, and a create whose entry here already exists writes over it rather than being refused as a duplicate. The index's key (its properties but $createdAt, and its terminal) must hold the whole key of an index a delete clears that skips no document. A value only such indexes use ($createdAt, when every index involving it outlives deletes) is neither carried by a delete nor part of the row commitment. Available from protocol version 14.

skipIfAbsent.description: Conditional participation: a document that omits a property of this index's skip set writes no entry into this index (and a delete, or on a stored type a replace, recomputes the same skip), so the index holds only documents carrying every skip property. `true` makes the skip set every optional property of the index; an array names the skip set (each must be one of the index's properties; an index has at most 10, hence maxItems). A skip property may sit at any position of the index, and must be a top-level schema property NOT listed in `required` (system properties are never optional), or, on a stored type and in the array form only, a derived index property (`<reference property>.<field>`) that can be absent: its reference property is optional, or the field is a schema property the referenced type does not require (nor every object around it); a document holding no value for it, null included, is skipped. On an indexOnly type the skip set must hold every optional property of the index (an index path has no representation for an absent value), every optional property needs a skip index whose skip set is that property alone, and at least one $createdAt-free index must remain non-skipIfAbsent (the executed-transition proof index); on a stored type the array may name a subset, the index's other optional properties keeping the null layout, and a skip index cannot be contested or set nullSearchable: false. No rankedCountable `at` level may sit above the deepest skip property. An absent property is distinct from an empty value: absence skips the index, while any present value — empty included — indexes normally. Available from protocol version 14.

summableOffCountIndex.description: Only on indexOnly document types: makes the index sum the count of another index. It names an index of the type, the source, and keeps per group of its own properties one counter holding the number of the source's entries in that group, with no entry per document. In the tree of the last property each group adds its counter, so its trees sum the source's entries in them, and with rangeCountable each group also counts one, so they count groups too: a count query over the index reads those sums, the source's entries, as does a sum query (which names the source index), and its average (with rangeCountable) is the entries per group. The sums are lossless: the source keeps entries, skips nothing, outlives no delete and involves no $createdAt; every source property is a property of this index; every other property of this index is a referring value of a `where` on a same-contract permanentDocument or moderatedDocument reference by id (no findBy or inList) held by a source property, to a value that never changes (the referenced $id or $creatorId, an $ownerId no transfer or purchase changes, or a property no replace or moderator can change: an unconditionally immutable one that is no optional deletableDocument reference by id (a replace may clear that once its document is deleted), or any of a documentsMutable: false type that no moderator's changeFields lists; kept on removal through moderatedDocument). This index may skip only on those other properties, needs rangeSummable: true, takes no terminal, summable, averageable, timeRange, integerRange or outlivesDelete, and is the only kind of index whose rankedSummable and rankedAverageable take the level-addressed form. Available from protocol version 14.

items.$comment: Every prerequisite here is sugar-aware, matching the structural parser, which expands `averageable` into `countable` + `summable` and `rangeAverageable` into `rangeCountable` + `rangeSummable` before it checks the same prerequisites on the resolved flags. `rangeSummable` accepts `averageable` or `summableOffCountIndex` in place of `summable`, and each `ranked*` flag accepts `rangeAverageable` in place of its own range axis (`rankedAverageable` also accepts the explicit `rangeCountable` + `rangeSummable` pair; `rankedCountable` on a summableOffCountIndex index needs no `rangeCountable`, being its Sum ranking). They are `if`/`then` pairs rather than `dependentRequired` rows only because `dependentRequired` cannot express the alternative. `rangeCountable` has no row at all: it implies `countable`, as it does at the doctype level, and the parser promotes an omitted `countable`. The remaining range rows keep the presence semantics they shipped with in v2 (an explicit `"rangeSummable": false` still needs a `summable` or an `averageable`); the ranked pairs are value-sensitive so that an explicit `"rankedCountable": false`, a written-out opt-out the structural parser accepts as such, demands nothing.

signatureSecurityLevelRequirement.description: Public key security level. 1 - Critical, 2 - High, 3 - Medium. If none specified, High level is used

documentsKeepHistory.description: True if the documents keep all their history, default is false

keepsTransferHistory.description: True if transfers of these documents are recorded in the document history system contract, default is false

keepsPurchaseHistory.description: True if purchases of these documents are recorded in the document history system contract, default is false

keepsPricingHistory.description: True if price updates on these documents are recorded in the document history system contract, default is false

documentsMutable.description: True if the documents are mutable, default is true

canBeDeleted.description: True if the documents' owners can delete them, default is the contract config's documentsCanBeDeletedContractDefault. "onlyWhenConsumed": the owner can not delete a document, but a create of the same contract whose refersTo declares consume deletes it, so the documents can still leave state and the type is a deletableDocument target, never a permanentDocument or moderatedDocument one. Refused on a type that keeps history or is indexOnly, whose documents nothing can consume. Fixed: an update may not change it. "onlyWhenConsumed" is available from protocol version 14.

transferable.description: Transferable without a marketplace sell. 0 - Never, 1 - Always

tradeMode.description: Built in marketplace system. 0 - None, 1 - Direct purchase (The user can buy the item without the need for an approval)

creationRestrictionMode.description: Restrictions of document creation. 0 - No restrictions, 1 - Owner only, 2 - No creation (System Only)

requiresIdentityEncryptionBoundedKey.description: Key requirements. 0 - Unique Non Replaceable, 1 - Multiple, 2 - Multiple with reference to latest key.

requiresIdentityDecryptionBoundedKey.description: Key requirements. 0 - Unique Non Replaceable, 1 - Multiple, 2 - Multiple with reference to latest key.

documentsCountable.description: When true, the primary key tree uses a CountTree enabling O(1) total document count queries.

rangeCountable.description: When true, the primary key tree uses a ProvableCountTree enabling range countable. Implies documentsCountable.

documentsSummable.description: Name of an integer document property aggregated into the primary-key SumTree (one sum per document type). Stores documents as `ItemWithSumItem` so the primary-key tree's root sum is the total of the named property across all docs of this type. Property must exist on the document type, be in `required`, and have an integer type. It must be a top-level property: the value is read from the top level of the document, so a dotted path to a property nested in an object is refused (from protocol version 14). Composes with `documentsKeepHistory: true` — keep-history doctypes get a `SumTree` per-document subtree with a `ReferenceWithSumItem` on the `0`-key carrying the current version's value, so the doctype-level root aggregate reflects current versions only (historical versions don't double-count).

rangeSummable.description: When true, the primary key tree uses a ProvableSumTree (or ProvableCountProvableSumTree paired with rangeCountable: true) enabling O(log n) range-sum queries over the primary axis. Requires `documentsSummable` to be set; `documentsAverageable` satisfies this, since it implies `documentsSummable`. Rarely useful — range-sum on the primary key with no where-clause filter is unusual; most callers want per-index `rangeSummable` instead. Set this only when you need a provable global range-sum tree.

documentsAverageable.description: Syntactic sugar: `documentsAverageable: "<prop>"` is shorthand for `documentsCountable: true` + `documentsSummable: "<prop>"`. Enables doctype-wide average queries (returns `(count, sum)` the client divides) without authors having to compose the count + sum flags. Same on-disk layout. If you set both `documentsAverageable` and `documentsSummable`, they must name the same property. Like `documentsSummable`, it names a top-level property, never a dotted path (from protocol version 14). Composes with `documentsKeepHistory: true` via the per-doc SumTree + ReferenceWithSumItem layout described under `documentsSummable`.

rangeAverageable.description: Syntactic sugar: `rangeAverageable: true` is shorthand for `rangeCountable: true` + `rangeSummable: true`. Requires `documentsAverageable` to be set. Same caveat as `rangeSummable` — rarely useful on the primary key; per-index `rangeAverageable` is what most callers want.

delete.description: When true, the contract's moderators (its owner and the identities its moderation config appoints, or its seated team) may delete documents of this type with a contract user moderation transition, leaving a removal record under the contract, and restore them. Independent of `canBeDeleted`, which rules what a document's own owner may do. Refused on a type that keeps history, is indexOnly, restricts document creation or has a contested index. For references a type carrying it is no longer permanent: a permanentDocument reference refuses it; a moderatedDocument reference is the one it takes when canBeDeleted is false, it declares no ttl and deleteKeepsRecord is not false, every document leaving state then leaving a removal record behind; a deletableDocument reference is the one it takes otherwise.

deleteWithin.description: For how many seconds after a document's last modification the moderators may still delete it. The last modification is the document's `$updatedAt`, or its `$createdAt` on a type that carries no `$updatedAt`. Once block time is later than that plus this many seconds the document is settled: no moderator can delete it alone any more, the contract owner included; `deleteSettled` may let the members of a seated team delete it together. A replace or a price update moves `$updatedAt` and opens the window again; a transfer, a purchase or a moderator's field change does not. Absent means no limit. Requires `delete: true` and `$updatedAt` in `required`; a type with `documentsMutable: false`, whose documents never change after their creation, may list `$createdAt` instead. Says nothing about what a document's own owner may do.

deleteKeepsRecord.description: Whether a moderator's deletion leaves a removal record under the contract: whose document it was, the moderator, the reason, the block time and a hash of the document, readable with getContractDocumentRemovals and never deleted. A deleted document can only be restored from its record, so false also means a deletion can not be undone, and the type has no removal records tree. A type keeping records whose owners can not delete their documents (canBeDeleted: false) and that declares no ttl is referred to by a moderatedDocument reference, which resolves to the record once the document is removed; false makes it a deletableDocument target. Default true. Requires `delete: true`.

deleteRefundsOwner.description: Whether the owner of a document a moderator deletes is refunded the part of its storage fee not yet paid out to past epochs, as an owner deleting it themselves is. Default false: the owner forfeits it, and the credits stay in the storage pools. A type with a `ttl` refunds nothing either way. Requires `delete: true`.

leader.description: Whether the seated team's leader must be among the approvals. Default false.

approvals.description: How many members of the seated team must approve, the leader counted among them. Default 1. At registration, at most the members the declared team can hold: its leader, the 15 members a charter elects and the elected declaration's maxAddedModerators.

approversPredateDocument.description: Whether a member the leader added (an addedModerator) proposes or approves the deletion of a document only when its addition was made before the document was created; one added in the same block does not count. The leader and the elected members always count. Without it, the leader could add members who approve whatever it proposes, and take them off again once they had. Default true when `approvals` is above 1 (false otherwise: a rule one approval meets, the leader meets alone), and true needs `$createdAt` in `required`. What the rule needs is not lowered for it: a team whose members from before a document are too few never deletes that document once settled. Every addition comes after the seat, so under a rule asking for more approvals than the leader and the members a charter elects, no document older than the seat is ever deleted once settled.

deleteSettled.description: Who must approve a moderator's deletion of a settled document, one past `deleteWithin`: a member of the contract's seated team proposes it with deleteSettledDocument, which is its own approval, the others approve the proposal by its action id with approveTeamAction, and the approval that meets the rule deletes the document, as `delete` would. `{"leader": true}` is the leader alone; `{"leader": true, "approvals": 3}` the leader and two others, any member the leader added among them added before the document was created unless `approversPredateDocument` is false. The proposals and their approvals are kept under the contract as team actions, readable with getContractTeamActions and getContractTeamActionSigners; nothing lapses, but an approval is refused once the document has changed since the proposal. Requires `deleteWithin` and a contract whose moderators are an elected team, which must give the team `deleteDocuments` on the type; no interim moderator deletes a settled document.

deleteKeepsFields.description: Property paths whose values a moderator's removal record keeps, copied from the document as it was deleted: what of the document stays public once it is gone (the hashtag of a removed post, say). Each entry names a declared property at any depth (`hashtag`, `meta.tags`, or an object kept whole), or one of the timestamps and block heights the type lists in `required` (`$createdAt`, `$updatedAtBlockHeight`, ...); not a transient property, not `$id` or `$ownerId` (every record holds them already), and not a path inside another listed one. A document without a value at a path leaves it out of the record. The values are read with the record (getContractDocumentRemovals), and the moderator pays for their storage. Requires `delete: true` and a record (`deleteKeepsRecord` not false).

changeFields.description: Top-level properties only the moderators write. A moderator sets or removes them with a contract user moderation transition (changeDocumentFields), which bumps `$revision` and leaves `$updatedAt` and every other property as it was. A document's owner can neither set them in a create nor change or remove them in a replace (DocumentModeratorFieldNotWritableError, code 41124), unless the owner moderates the contract. Every entry must name a declared top-level property that is optional, not transient, not listed under `immutable`, neither a reference nor read by one (a where value, a findBy source or function param, a key id), neither generated nor read by a generated property, and in no contested index; refused on an indexOnly type. A type listing any keeps `$revision` on its documents even when `documentsMutable` is false.

moderatorAbilities.description: What the contract's moderators may do to documents of this type with a contract user moderation transition: delete them (`delete`, within `deleteWithin` seconds of their last modification when given, leaving a removal record unless `deleteKeepsRecord` is false, keeping in it the values `deleteKeepsFields` lists, refunding the owner when `deleteRefundsOwner` is true), and write the fields only they write (`changeFields`). Requires the contract to declare `moderation` in its config. Fixed when the document type is created: an update may not add, remove or change it. Available from protocol version 14.

ttl.description: Time to live, in seconds: the platform deletes each document of this type once its `$createdAt` plus this many seconds has passed, whoever owns it and whatever `canBeDeleted` says, at most a protocol-versioned number of documents per block (128 at protocol version 14) after the block's state transitions. Its documents are stored without storage flags and refund nothing when deleted: instead of the perpetual storage price, each byte they write pays a price for the time they will live (five tiers up to seven days, then per 9.125 days spanned), paid out as storage fees to the epochs they live in (at most one era of them), and a document prepays its deletion as processing when it is created. From its expiry on, a document can no longer be replaced, transferred, bought, repriced or restored by a moderator; its owner may still delete it where `canBeDeleted` allows. Requires `$createdAt` in `required`; refused together with `documentsKeepHistory`, `indexOnly` and a contested index. A `permanentDocument` reference, one found by `findBy` or with `inList` included, and a `moderatedDocument` reference may not target the type; a `deletableDocument` reference, one found by `findBy` included, may. At least and at most protocol-versioned bounds (3600, one hour, and 31536000, one year, at protocol version 14). Fixed when the document type is created: an update may not add, remove or change it. Available from protocol version 14.

indexOnly.description: When true, documents of this type are never written to primary storage: the index entries are the rows, each terminating in an Item keyed by the index's `terminal` property instead of a Reference keyed by the document id. Only what is in the indexes exists and is recoverable. Requires: every property required and appearing in at least one index (except a skip property of a `skipIfAbsent` index, which may be optional), $ownerId in at least one index (as a property or terminal), documentsMutable: false, no transfers/trading/history/transient properties, and no doctype-level aggregate keywords (use the index-level count flags). Available from protocol version 14.

entryPayload.description: Only on indexOnly document types: the top-level properties stored in every entry's value, after the 32-byte row commitment, instead of in a key — the type's value slot. Each is length-framed in property-name order and recovered by decoding the proved element: raw bytes for byte arrays, UTF-8 for strings, and tree-key encoding for other scalars. Empty byte arrays and strings remain distinct from null, and an empty string remains distinct from a NUL string. Listed properties must be required, bounded (maxItems on byte arrays, maxLength on strings), scalar, and must not appear in any index as a property or a terminal component; their summed bounds are capped by the field value limit. With more than one index the payload rides in every entry. Fixed when the document type is created. Available from protocol version 14.

actionFees.description: A fixed fee in credits charged, on top of the gas, for actions on documents of this type, split between the contract's owner pot and its moderators pot (each paid out by a ContractFeeClaim state transition). Whoever pays the gas of the action pays its fee. A transition on a priced action must name the declared owner and moderators amounts, and for feeMultiplier pricing the fee multiplier its signer knew with the increase in percent they accept, in $actionFeeAgreement; it is refused without one (DocumentActionFeeAgreementNotSetError, code 40132), with other amounts or another pricing (code 40133), or when the epoch's multiplier rose beyond the accepted increase (code 40134). At least one action must be priced and a priced action must charge something. Fixed when the document type is published: a contract update cannot add, change or remove the fees of an existing document type. Available from protocol version 14.

pricing.description: feeMultiplier (default): the declared amounts are scaled by the fee multiplier of the epoch the action executes in. fixed: the declared amounts are charged as written.

transient.description: Names of top-level properties whose values are validated on the transition but never stored: a create, and from protocol version 14 a replace, drops them before the document is written. From protocol version 14 every entry must name a top-level property (list the object around a nested one); no index may read a transient property or one inside a transient object; a refersTo findBy may not read one on either side (a findBy function's params may), a where may not name one on its referenced side, and a stored key id may not pair with a transient identity; encryptedFor may not name one; generatedFrom may neither name one nor sit on one. Adding, removing or changing an entry on contract update is an incompatible schema change.

immutable.description: The top-level properties of a mutable document type a replace may not change, add or remove. An entry naming a property freezes it at document creation; an entry { "property": ..., "when": condition } freezes it for any replace the condition holds for, and leaves it free for any other. A condition takes the grammar of a propertyConstraints rule (comparisons, arithmetic, in, present, absent, anyOf, allOf, not, ifThen, ifThenElse, the system times and heights the type requires, $ownerId) and is judged on the document the replace writes: its $updatedAt is the replace's block time, so { "greaterThan": [{ "subtract": ["$updatedAt", "$createdAt"] }, 300000] } freezes a property five minutes after the document was created. A path under $old. reads the stored document instead: { "present": "$old.trackingCode" } lets an absent trackingCode be set once, and { "equal": ["$old.status", { "const": "published" }] } freezes a property once the stored document is published. A condition may read no countOf or sumOf total. A replace changing a frozen property is rejected (DocumentImmutablePropertyChangedError, code 40128), except one removing a refersTo deletableDocument reference by id, listed without a condition, whose referenced document has been deleted. Only allowed when documentsMutable is true (the default). Every property must be a declared top-level property that is not transient, listed once: system properties ($-prefixed) are excluded because the platform manages them, and nested paths are not accepted (list the containing object to freeze it whole). A deletableDocument reference by id may be listed only without a condition. On contract update a property may be added, with a condition or without, and one listed with a condition may lose it; one listed without a condition stays, a condition never changes, and no property is dropped. Replaces immutableAllowSetting, which is refused. Available from protocol version 14.

retractedWhen.description: The condition under which a replace writes a retracted document: on a moderated contract, the one replace a banned or suspended owner may still make. A barred owner can write nothing new, but may still delete its documents and, on a type declaring retractedWhen, replace one when the document the replace writes meets the condition; any other replace by it is refused with ContractUserBannedError (41107) or ContractUserSuspendedError (41108). So an author whose documents can not be deleted (canBeDeleted: false) can still take back what it wrote. The condition is an immutable entry's when: the grammar of a propertyConstraints rule, judged on the document the replace writes, with the stored document read through $old., and no countOf or sumOf. A condition that cannot be evaluated counts as not met. What a retracted document holds is for the type's other rules to say: { "present": "deleted" } with a propertyConstraints rule that a document carrying deleted carries no content, and an immutable entry { "property": "deleted", "when": { "present": "$old.deleted" } } that keeps it retracted. Only allowed when documentsMutable is true and the contract keeps a banlist or a suspension list. Adding, removing or changing it on contract update is an incompatible change. Available from protocol version 14.

ownerRefersTo.description: A refersTo declaration whose value is the document's $ownerId, the writer, instead of a property's value: the declaration of an identifier property, with the same keys and the same checks, for the targets a writer can be: identity, a permanentDocument or a deletableDocument found by findBy, where "." is the writer, or a permanentDocument with inList, the writer an element of the list, or an anyOf or allOf expression whose every leaf is one of them and "$ownerId" names the writer as well. A deletableDocument leaf gates the writer on the document findBy finds existing now: every replace checks it again, so a writer whose document is gone can no longer replace theirs (it may still delete it). contract, token and a document by id are refused, since the writer's identity id is never one of those ids, and identityPublicKey pairs the value with a key id, which the writer does not carry. A where value is still a property of the document or its $ownerId, the same writer. Only on a document type whose documents can be neither transferred nor traded, so the writer stays the owner; on a type whose documents can, creatorRefersTo checks the creator instead. When a document is created, and when a replace changes a property findBy or where reads (every replace for a where value $ownerId), consensus checks the writer against the target exactly as a property's value is checked, and refuses the write with the error that target reports for a property (ReferencedEntityNotFoundError, 40120, and the rest), naming $ownerId as the path. It counts as one reference against the references a document may carry. Fixed when the document type is created: adding, removing or changing it is an incompatible schema change on update. Available from protocol version 14.

creatorRefersTo.description: A refersTo declaration whose value is the document's $creatorId, its creator, instead of a property's value: the counterpart of ownerRefersTo for a document type whose documents can be transferred or traded, since the creator never changes. The declaration of an identifier property, with the same keys and the same checks, for the targets a creator can be: identity, a permanentDocument found by findBy, where "." is the creator, a permanentDocument with inList, the creator an element of the list, a deletableDocument found by a findBy function (a commitment the creator reveals, checked when the document is created only, see findBy), or an anyOf or allOf expression whose every leaf is one of them. contract, token, a document by id and any other deletableDocument (the creator never changes, and a document a transfer handed on could not be replaced once the one findBy found is deleted) are refused, since the creator's identity id is never one of those ids, and identityPublicKey pairs the value with a key id, which the creator does not carry. A where value is still a property of the document or its $ownerId, the writer. Only on a document type that records creator ids: a transferable or tradeable document type of a format-1 contract; a type declares at most one of ownerRefersTo and creatorRefersTo. When a document is created (by its creator) and when a replace changes a property findBy or where reads (every replace for a where value $ownerId), consensus checks the creator against the target exactly as a property's value is checked, and refuses the write with the error that target reports for a property (ReferencedEntityNotFoundError, 40120, and the rest), naming $creatorId as the path. A transfer or a purchase needs no check: it does not change the creator. It counts as one reference against the references a document may carry. Fixed when the document type is created: adding, removing or changing it is an incompatible schema change on update. Available from protocol version 14.

propertyConstraints.description: Rules every created or replaced document of the type must meet, by name (1 to 64 letters, digits or underscores). A rule is a condition: an object with one key, either a comparison (equal, notEqual, lessThan, lessThanOrEqual, greaterThan or greaterThanOrEqual) listing the two integer expressions it compares, left then right, equal or notEqual of the path of a string property and a const string ({ "equal": ["status", { "const": "closed" }] }, either way round) or of the paths of two string properties, which compares their strings, and likewise for identifier properties, whose constants are base58 identifiers, in listing an integer expression and two or more distinct integer values it may take or the path of a string property and two or more distinct strings, startsWith or endsWith listing two strings, a const or a string property each, at least one a property, and holding if the first starts or ends with the second, byte for byte (a constant looked for in a string property that declares enum must start or end one of its values), contains listing the path of a typed array property and the value one of its elements must equal (an integer expression among integers, a const string or string property among strings, a const base58 identifier, identifier property or $ownerId among identifiers; an array left out holds nothing, and a constant must be one of the elements' enum values when they declare one), present or absent naming a property of any type (the document holds it, or leaves it out or sets it to null), or anyOf, allOf, not, ifThen or ifThenElse over conditions: anyOf holds if at least one of its two or more conditions holds, allOf if every one does, not if its one condition does not, ifThen if its second condition holds whenever its first does (the second evaluated only then), ifThenElse if its second holds when its first does and its third when it does not (only that branch evaluated); notIn lists what in lists and holds if the expression takes none of the values. An expression is an integer value, the dotted path of an integer or boolean property of the document type, whose value it takes (a boolean reading as 1 for true and 0 for false), 0 when the document leaves it out, a system time or height the document type records by listing it in required ($createdAt, $updatedAt and $transferredAt, block times in milliseconds, and each with BlockHeight or CoreBlockHeight appended, the Platform and Core block heights: those of the create, of the last create, replace or price update, and of the last create, transfer or purchase), or an object with one key: ifAbsent, a property path and the value it takes when the document leaves it out (an integer, or a string for a string property compared with strings); add, multiply, min or max, two or more operands; subtract, divide, modulo or power, exactly two; abs, one; length or byteLength, the characters or UTF-8 bytes of a string property, or count, the items of an array or byte array property, each 0 when the document leaves the property out ({ "lessThanOrEqual": [{ "count": "tags" }, "maxTags"] }); countOf or sumOf, how many documents of a document type of this contract match a filter (keys of that type or $ownerId, each mapped to a value read from the document written, $id its id) or the total of an integer property over them, as that type's count or sum trees keep it once the write is done, which needs documentsCountable or documentsSummable for a whole type and otherwise an index whose properties are exactly the filter's keys ({ "lessThanOrEqual": [{ "countOf": ["listing", { "$ownerId": "$ownerId" }] }, 10] }). A string property the document leaves out equals no constant and no other string property, not even one also left out, unless an ifAbsent gives it a string default ({ "ifAbsent": ["status", "open"] }), which it then reads as, and a constant compared with a string property that declares enum must be one of its values. The arithmetic is exact over 128-bit signed integers, operands evaluated left to right: divide and modulo are Euclidean (the remainder is never negative), 0 to the power 0 is 1, and a value or intermediate result that does not fit, a zero divisor, a negative exponent or a property value that is not an integer breaks the rule. Conditions are checked in declared order and no further than the outcome needs (anyOf stops at the first that holds, allOf at the first that fails), and a fault met in a condition that is checked breaks the rule whatever the others would say (not does not turn it into a pass), so an earlier condition can guard a later one. Every property an operand reads must be an integer or boolean property, every property length or byteLength measures a string property, every property count counts an array or byte array property, every property compared with a string a string property, present and absent may test a property of any type, and no property a rule reads may be transient or inside a transient object; every comparison and in must read at least one property, an anyOf or allOf may not hold two alike conditions or directly another of its kind, a not may not hold directly another not or a notIn, a literal 0 divisor or negative exponent is refused, and no condition or operand may nest deeper than 64 levels; a type declares at most SystemLimits max_property_constraints rules (16 from protocol version 14) of at most max_property_constraint_nodes nodes each (32), counting every comparison and logical operator, every in and each value it lists, every contains and its array, every const, every present or absent, every arithmetic operator and every operand, a size included; all checked at contract registration. When a document is created or replaced, consensus checks every rule, in name order, after the schema validation, and refuses the first one the document breaks (DocumentPropertyConstraintViolatedError, 10422). $ownerId, the document's owner, is an identifier operand (never a property: not in present, absent or an integer operand, and not on an indexOnly type), and a transfer or a purchase, which gives the document a new owner, is refused when it would break a rule reading it. Likewise a transfer or a purchase is judged against the rules reading the transfer's time and heights, and a price update against those reading the update's, since each sets them; an indexOnly type reads no system time or height. The rules change nothing stored, and read state only for countOf and sumOf, each total a billed read of a count or sum tree, at most max_property_constraint_aggregates distinct totals per type (4); a type with a contested index totals no documents of its own type, since a document a contest awards is stored without the rules judged. Fixed when the document type is created: adding, removing or changing a rule is an incompatible schema change on update. Available from protocol version 14.

deleteConstraints.description: Rules the stored document must meet for its owner to delete it, by name (1 to 64 letters, digits or underscores), in the grammar of a propertyConstraints rule and held to the same limits, counted apart from propertyConstraints (16 rules of 32 nodes each, reading 4 distinct totals). When the owner deletes a document, consensus checks every rule, in name order, against the stored document (its properties, its $ownerId, the system times and heights the type requires, as stored) and refuses the delete at the first rule it breaks (DocumentDeleteConstraintViolatedError, 40147), paid. A countOf or sumOf reads the total as it will be once the document is gone, so a rule over the type's own documents no longer counts it, and a filter may match by the document's own id: { "noVotes": { "equal": [{ "countOf": ["vote", { "pollId": "$id" }] }, 0] } } lets a poll be deleted only while no vote points at it. Only the owner's delete is judged: the contract's moderators and a ttl delete as before. Only on a document type whose owner may delete its documents (canBeDeleted true, not "onlyWhenConsumed") and that is not indexOnly, and a refersTo with consume may not target the type, since a consume deletes without the rules. Fixed when the document type is created: adding, removing or changing a rule is an incompatible schema change on update. Available from protocol version 14.

allOf.$comment: `documentsAverageable` is sugar for `documentsCountable` + `documentsSummable`, so it satisfies `rangeSummable`'s prerequisite exactly as `documentsSummable` does; an `if`/`then` pair because `dependentRequired` cannot express the alternative, with the presence semantics the row shipped with in v2.
